title: Scenario Lab: model substitution triggers and procurement playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Run a cross-regional scenario lab that operationalizes procurement-trigger thresholds for model substitution. The goal is to produce a pragmatic playbook that product, infra, and procurement teams can use when a primary model becomes degraded/unavailable, or when economics (cost/latency) cross a threshold. Deliverables: 1) decision matrix tying model availability, latency delta, and per-token cost delta to specific procurement actions (e.g., activate reserved capacity, source alternative model variant, escalate to procurement), 2) recommended telemetry signals and thresholds (SLO breaches, 99th/95th p99 latency windows, cost spikes, regional capacity loss), 3) synthetic probes and a small field pilot that simulates outages and switches traffic to fallbacks, 4) buyer-journey prototypes that show enterprise procurement timelines and contract clauses required for rapid model switches, 5) list of instrumentation and console dashboards needed to make decisions within SLA windows.
acceptance_criteria: A decision matrix (CSV) linking signal combinations to runnable actions exists and is reviewed by Eng and Procurement
A small synthetic workload runner (doc + runbook) can reproduce 3 substitution scenarios and shows expected latency/cost impact
Telemetry spec and dashboard mocks are created in Console and approved by Observability team
Procurement playbook draft including contract language for fallback model substitutions is reviewed by Legal and Procurement
Pilot run (internal only) completed for two regions (us-west and ap-southeast) showing automated fallback within target window
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff with Eng, Procurement, Legal. Collected initial hypothesis list and historical outage traces.
2025-02-20: Built first decision-matrix prototype mapping (latency delta, cost delta, availability impact) -> action tier. Shared with Observability for feedback.
2025-02-24: Observability requested additional signal: 15m rolling token-cost rate and model-variant landing-rate. Added to telemetry spec.
2025-02-26: Draft procurement clause for emergency substitution under reserved capacity prepared; Legal flagged two compliance review items.
2025-02-28: Synthetic probe harness (python script) initial run shows expected 20% latency uplift when switching to quantized fallback for long-tail queries.
2025-03-01: Scope refined: pilot limited to hosted + dedicated combo; removed on-prem pilot due to infra constraints this quarter. Updated estimate to 8 points.
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: prefer automated fallback for latency-first customers, manual approval for high-cost substitution for enterprise customers
APAC considerations: regional model availability is more volatile; include region-specific thresholds and procurement contacts
Follow-up: schedule a tabletop exercise with two customer success leads and one major enterprise account to validate timing assumptions
